W5 (contrarian), after E020.
1. Noise. Rebuilding the same commit only reshuffles results slightly: E017 and E019 (both dddcf96) gave 0.7537 and 0.7541. A change to kernels or graphs acts like a fresh 3-seed draw: E015, E016 and E017 share the same math and spread from 0.7537 to 0.7607. I put the per-seed SD at about 0.4 pp and the 3-seed SD at about 0.25 pp. My estimate of the tip's true mean is about 0.756, which leaves about 0.3 pp of real margin. The tip's local reading of 0.7537 is a low draw. E016's 0.7607 was a high draw, and the wd cut itself is close to neutral; filter wd is inert anyway.
2. The epoch dial is flatter than I thought. E020 cut one true epoch (238→213 steps) and saved 10.5% of time (6.55→5.86 s). Measured accuracy was 0.7528, about 0.3 pp below the tip's true mean, so the cost is about 0.15 pp per 0.5 epoch. That is the best time-for-accuracy rate seen so far, about 2.3 s per pp. E020 missed the bar narrowly, partly through bad luck. Every other lever has to beat that rate.
3. Mechanism others miss: the final-map regime, not pixels. The 2x2 valid stem plus three pools give a 3×3 final map at 28 and 32 px but only 2×2 at 20 and 24 px. Accuracy tracks the absolute number of steps trained in the 3×3 regime late in the schedule, at low LR:
- E018 moved 30% of steps from 28 to 24 px, the 3×3 regime to 2×2, and lost about 0.5 pp for 8.5% of time. That rate is worse than the epoch dial.
- E011 cut both and fell off a cliff.
- E020 shrank the 32 px tail proportionally and cost little.

So time spent in the 2×2 regime is cheap to cut, and 3×3-regime steps are expensive. Untested lever: 26 px (25→12→6→3) replacing 28 px keeps the 3×3 regime at about 0.66 of 32 px cost instead of 0.77, saving about 4% of time for little accuracy.
4. Time is about proportional to weighted pixel-MACs, with fixed overhead ≤0.3 s. The E011 and E018 savings were close to or slightly above pixel-proportional. MACs at 32 px split 20/51/29% across groups 1/2/3. Narrowing group 2 to 320 removes about 15.6% of MACs (part of it in group 3's conv1). Dropping group 1's conv3 removes about 7.3%.
5. Capacity on CIFAR-100: about 0.35 pp per 11% of last-group width (E010). Group 2 is likely just as width-hungry, so cutting it costs about 0.4–0.6 pp for about 9% of time. That is no better than the epoch dial. Depth in group 1 is cheaper in time, but its accuracy cost is uncertain.
6. Code facts: Muon renormalizes the filters, so filter wd is inert. It runs 3 Newton-Schulz steps. The tip has 238 true steps (9.5 epochs). BN momentum is effectively 0.4, so the running stats track only the last few batches and BN recalibration should be worth little.
Unsure: the held-out 10-seed mean from E019 (not shown to me), whether the 26 px or 30 px tail ideas work, and the true epoch slope (one point, noisy).
Best path: a trim of about 0.5 epoch, ideally while keeping the 3×3-regime step count, plus a cheap swap of the early 24 px phase for 20 px.

forecasts.reason: About 15.6% fewer MACs gives about 8–10% less time, but a width-hungry 100-class stage likely costs more than 0.25 pp against E016's high draw. The time-for-accuracy rate is no better than the epoch dial.
Filter wd is inert and E016's gain was mostly noise; reaching 0.763 (+0.2 pp over E016) is unlikely.
About 7% of MACs plus some BN/GELU gives about 6–7% less time, short of the 8% threshold; the accuracy loss is likely 0.3–0.6 pp.
The swapped steps are in the 2×2 regime either way, so accuracy should be nearly free. The time saving is about 3.5–4%, right at the threshold.

cruxes: What 10-seed held-out mean did E019 record for the tip: about 0.756, or nearer 0.760? This sets how much trim the margin can fund.
Is accuracy set by steps in the 3×3 final-map regime (28/32 px)? Test: a −0.5 epoch trim taken only from the 2×2-regime (24 px) phase, versus E020's uniform cut, plus 26 px replacing 28 px.
Is the epoch slope truly about 0.15 pp per 0.5 epoch (E020)? If so, a −0.5 epoch trim (about 6.2 s) is the best next move over any architecture FLOP cut.
